title: Thought Experiments
desc: Paradoxes, probability traps & the experiments that broke physics

questions.q: Schrödinger's cat is both alive and dead — but what was Schrödinger actually trying to prove with the thought experiment?
questions.a: That the Copenhagen interpretation of quantum mechanics was absurd — it was a criticism, not a celebration of the idea

questions.q: The 'Monty Hall problem': you pick door 1, the host opens door 3 (a goat). Should you switch to door 2?
questions.a: Yes — switching gives you a 2/3 chance of winning. Staying is only 1/3. Even professional mathematicians argued about this

questions.q: What is an 'island of stability' in nuclear physics?
questions.a: A predicted group of superheavy elements that might be stable enough to exist for more than fractions of a second — we haven't confirmed any yet

questions.q: The twin paradox: if one twin travels near light speed and returns, what happens?
questions.a: The travelling twin ages less — this isn't a paradox, it's confirmed by special relativity. GPS satellites experience this daily and must correct for it

questions.q: What is 'quantum entanglement' in plain English?
questions.a: Two particles become linked so that measuring one instantly determines the state of the other, regardless of distance — Einstein called it 'spooky action at a distance'

questions.q: The Bechdel test is used for films — but which scientific field has an equivalent test for research papers?
questions.a: There isn't a direct equivalent — this is a trick question. The Bechdel test is purely a film/media metric

questions.q: What is a 'quasar' and why can we see them from billions of light-years away?
questions.a: An extremely luminous core of a distant galaxy powered by a supermassive black hole consuming matter — they can outshine their entire host galaxy

questions.q: Why is a year on Mercury only 88 Earth days, but a single day on Mercury lasts 59 Earth days?
questions.a: Mercury rotates very slowly on its axis but orbits the Sun quickly — so a Mercurian day is about 2/3 of its year

questions.q: The 'ship of Theseus' asks: if you replace every plank of a ship, is it the same ship? Which modern technology faces this exact philosophical problem?
questions.a: Your own body — nearly every cell is replaced over 7-10 years. Also: software that's been entirely rewritten over time

questions.q: What is 'dark matter' and what's the best evidence for it?
questions.a: Invisible matter that doesn't interact with light but exerts gravitational pull — galaxies rotate too fast to be held together by visible matter alone
